Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 1
, Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly concluded that Option B is balanced without performing a rigorous verification of the Oxygen atoms. In Option B ($C_{2}H_{6} + 5O_{2} \rightarrow 2CO_{2} + 3H_{2}O$), the left side has 10 oxygen atoms ($5 \times 2$), while the right side has 10 oxygen atoms ($2 \times 2 + 3 \times 1$). Wait, let me re-calculate.
Left: $C_2H_6$ (0 O) + $5O_2$ (10 O) = 10 O.
Right: $2CO_2$ (4 O) + $3H_2O$ (3 O) = 7 O.
The Planner's calculation in the "Analysis of Previous Result" section states: "Right has 2 CO2 (4 O) + 3 H2O (6 O) = 10 O". This is the error. The agent incorrectly calculated the oxygen atoms in water ($H_2O$) as 6 instead of 3 ($3 \times 1$). Consequently, the Planner falsely identified Option B as balanced when it is not (it violates conservation of mass). Option D ($2C_{2}H_{6} + 7O_{2} \rightarrow 4CO_{2} + 6H_{2}O$) is actually the correct balanced equation. The Planner's arithmetic error led to the wrong final answer.
